Formerly, Mí Zǐxiá was favored by the ruler of Wèi.

The ruler heard of it and praised him, saying:
"How filial!
For the sake of his mother, he risked the crime of amputation!"
Once, while strolling in the orchard with the ruler,
Mí Zǐ ate a peach that was sweet,
and not finishing it, he presented it to the ruler.
The ruler said:
"Love me,
forget his words but remember me!"
When Mí Zǐxiá's 彌子瑕 beauty faded and love waned,
he offended the ruler.
The ruler said:
"He once presumptuously drove my carriage,
and once fed me with his leftover peach."
Therefore, Mí Zǐ's 彌子 behavior had not changed from the beginning,
but the reason he was seen as virtuous before and then guilty afterward
was the extreme change in love and hate.
Therefore, if one is loved by the ruler,
then when he is deemed correct, intimacy increases;
if one is hated by the ruler,
then even when the crime fits the punishment, estrangement increases.
Therefore, those who offer remonstrations and advice must carefully observe the ruler's love and hate before speaking to him.
Now, the dragon, as a creature,
can be tamed and ridden.
However, under its throat, it has reverse scales, one foot in diameter;
if a person touches them,
it will surely kill the person.
Rulers also have reverse scales;
if those who advise him can avoid touching the ruler's reverse scales,

"Biography of Sima Rangju, Number Four"
Sima Rangju was a descendant of Tian Wan.
Tián Wán zhī miáoyì yě.
During the time of Duke Jing of Qi,
Jin attacked A and
Zhen, while Yan invaded the area north of the Yellow River,
and the Qi army suffered a crushing defeat.
Duke Jing was troubled by this.
Yan Ying then recommended Tian Rangju, saying:
"Rangju, although an illegitimate son of the Tian family,
his personal qualities can win over the people,
and his military skills can intimidate the enemy.
I hope you will try him."
Duke Jing summoned Rangju,
and spoke with him about military matters,
and was greatly pleased with him.
He appointed him as general,
to lead the army to defend against the Yan and Jin forces.
Rangju said:
"Your subject has always been of humble status.
You, my lord, have raised me from the ranks of commoners,
elevating me above the rank of grandee.
The soldiers are not yet attached to me,
and the people do not trust me.
My influence is weak and my authority is light.
I hope to have a favorite minister of yours,
The state respects those who
can oversee the army,
only then is it acceptable."
Thereupon, Duke Jǐng agreed to it
and sent Zhuāng Jiǎ.
Rǎng Jū having taken his leave,
made an agreement with Zhuāng Jiǎ, saying:
"At noon tomorrow, we will meet at the gate of the camp."
Rǎng Jū first hurried to the camp,
erected a marker and used a water clock to await Jiǎ.
Jiǎ was usually arrogant and noble,
thinking that he would be commanding his own army and that he was the overseer,
he was not very anxious;
relatives and attendants saw him off,
detaining him for drinks.
Noon came, but Jiǎ did not arrive.
Rǎng Jū then knocked over the marker and released the water clock,
entered, inspected the troops and tightened discipline,
clearly declaring the regulations.
Once the regulations were established,
in the evening,
Zhuāng Jiǎ finally arrived.
Rǎng Jū said:
"Why are you late?"
Jiǎ apologized, saying:
"Your unworthy servant was seen off by relatives of the senior officials,
so I was delayed."
Rǎng Jū said:
"On the day one receives a commission, one forgets one's family;
when facing the army and issuing commands, one forgets one's relatives;
when seizing the drumsticks in a critical situation, one forgets oneself.
Now, the enemy state deeply invades,
the country is in turmoil,
soldiers are exposed on the borders,
the ruler sleeps uneasily,
eats without savor,
the lives of the people are all hanging on the ruler.
What is this talk of seeing me off!"
Zhào Jū 召居 questioned the military law officer, saying:
"What is the punishment according to military law for those who arrive after the appointed time?"
He replied:
"They should be executed."
Zhuāng Jiǎ 莊賈 was afraid
and sent someone to rush a message to Jǐng Gōng 景公,
requesting help.
After he left,
before he could return,
thereupon Zhāng Jiǎ 莊賈 was executed as a warning to the three armies.
The soldiers of the three armies all trembled.
After a long time,
Jǐng Gōng 景公 sent a messenger holding a token of pardon for Jiǎ 賈,
rushing into the army camp.
Ráng Jū 穰苴 said:
"When a general is in the army,
there are commands from the ruler that need not be obeyed."
He asked the military law officer:
"What is the law for rushing through the three armies?"
Zhèng said:
"It warrants beheading."
The messenger was greatly afraid.
Ráng Jū said:
"The ruler's messenger cannot be killed."
Thereupon, he beheaded his servant,
the left brace of the chariot,
and the left horse of the team,
to display them throughout the three armies.
He sent the messenger back to report,
and then he marched.
He personally inquired about the soldiers' accommodations, wells, cooking stoves, food, drink, illnesses, and medicine,
personally comforting and caring for them.
He took all of the general's provisions and supplies to share with the soldiers,
dividing the food equally with the soldiers,
especially caring for the weakest among them.
Only after three days did he muster the troops.
The sick all asked to go into battle,
vying to rush out and fight for him.
When the Jìn army heard of this,
they withdrew.
When the Yān army heard of this,
they crossed the river and disbanded.
Thereupon, he pursued and attacked them,
and recovered the lost territory within the borders and then led his army home.
Before reaching the capital,
he disbanded the army,
He dissolved the restraints,
took oaths and covenants, and then entered the city.
Jǐng Gōng and the assembled officials greeted him in the suburbs,
rewarded the army and completed the ceremonies,
and then returned to his chambers.
Having met Rǎng Jū,
he honored him as Grand Marshal (Dà Sīmǎ).
The Tián family became increasingly honored in Qí.
Later, the officials of the Bào family,
and the families of Gāo and Guó became jealous of him,
and slandered him to Jǐng Gōng.
Jǐng Gōng dismissed Rǎng Jū,
and Jū developed an illness and died.
The followers of Tián Qǐ and
Tián Bào thus harbored resentment against the families of Gāo and
Guó.
Later, Tián Cháng went so far as to assassinate Duke Jiǎn,
completely exterminating the clans of Gāo Zǐ and
Guó Zǐ.
By the time of Cháng's great-grandson, Hé,
he then established himself as King Wēi of Qí.
He used military force and exercised his power,

King Wēi of Qí ordered his officials to trace and discuss the ancient *Sīmǎ's Art of War* and attach Rǎng Jū's principles to it,
therefore it was called *Sīmǎ Rǎng Jū's Art of War*.

"Biography of Sūnzǐ and Wúqǐ, Number Five"
Sūnzǐ Wǔ was a man of Qí.
Qí rén yě.
He presented his art of war to King Hélǘ of Wú.
Hélǘ said:
"Your thirteen chapters,
I have read them all.
Can I try a small exercise in troop discipline?"
He replied:
"You can."
Hélǘ said:
"Can I try it with women?"
He said:
"You can."
So he agreed to it and brought out beauties from the palace,
chū gōngzhōng měinǚ,
totaling one hundred and eighty people.
Sūnzǐ divided them into two squads,
with the king's two most favored concubines each as a team leader,
ordering them all to hold halberds.
He instructed them, saying:
"Do you understand the difference between your chest, left hand, right hand, and back?"
The women said:
"We understand."
Sūnzǐ said:
"For 'forward,'
look at your chest;
for 'left,' look at your left hand;
for 'right,' look at your right hand;
for 'backward,' look at your back."
The women said:
"Yes."
Once the rules were established,
he then set up axes and execution blocks,
and proceeded to explain the orders repeatedly.
Thereupon, he beat the drum to signal 'right,'
and the women laughed loudly.
Sūnzǐ said:
"If the rules are not clear
and the orders are not thoroughly explained,
"It is the general's fault."
He repeated the orders and instructions three and five times and then drummed to the left,
and the women again laughed loudly.
Sūnzǐ said:
"If the regulations are not clear,

it is the general's fault;
if they are already clear but not followed according to the law,

Thereupon, he wanted to execute the left and right squad leaders.
The King of Wú watched from the platform,

The women, left and right, front and back, kneeling and rising, all met the standards of the compass and plumb line,

Thereupon Sūnzǐ sent a messenger to report to the King, saying:
“Now that the soldiers are fully organized,

King Wú said:

Sūnzǐ said:

Thereupon, Hélǘ knew that Sūnzǐ was capable in military affairs,

To the west, he defeated the powerful Chǔ,

After Sūn Wǔ died,

Bìn was born between Ā and Juàn,

Sūn Bìn once studied military strategy together with Páng Juān.

When Bìn arrived,

An envoy from Qí 齊 went to Liáng 梁.
Sūn Bìn 孫臏, as a criminal serving his sentence, secretly met with the Qí 齊 envoy,

The Qí 齊 envoy thought him extraordinary,

The Qí 齊 general Tián Jì 田忌 treated him well and as a guest.
Jì 忌 frequently raced horses and wagered heavily with the various sons of the Qí 齊 ruler.
Sūnzi 孫子 saw that the quality of their horses was not very different,

middle, and lower grades.
Thereupon Sūnzi 孫子 said to Tián Jì 田忌:
"Your Lordship, please wager heavily,
I can make Your Lordship win."
Tián Jì 田忌 believed him,

When it came time to compete,
Sūnzi 孫子 said:
"Now, use Your Lordship's lower-grade horses against their upper-grade horses,
use Your Lordship's upper-grade horses against their middle-grade horses,

After the three rounds were finished,
Tián Jì 田忌 lost one and won two,

Therefore, Jì recommended Sūnzǐ to King Wēi.
King Wēi inquired about military strategy,

Later, Wèi attacked Zhào.
Zhào was in distress

King Wēi of Qí intended to appoint Sūn Bìn as the general,

Consequently, he appointed Tián Jì as the general,

Tián Jì intended to lead the troops to Zhào,

"To unravel a tangled mess, one doesn't pull on the knot.
To rescue those fighting, one doesn't engage in the brawl.
Strike at their vulnerable points, exploit their weaknesses;
creating a situation of constraint and prohibition,

Now, Liáng and Zhào are attacking each other;
their elite troops will certainly be exhausted outside,

You would do better to lead your troops quickly to Dàliáng,
seize its thoroughfares,

they will certainly abandon Zhào and save themselves.
"This is how I can lift the siege of Zhào in one fell swoop and collect the spoils from Wèi."
Tián Jì followed his advice.
Wèi indeed withdrew from Hándān.
They fought with Qí at Guìlíng.
They greatly defeated the Liáng army.
Thirteen years later,
Wèi and Zhào attacked Hán.
Hán urgently appealed to Qí.
Qí sent Tián Jì as general to go there,

The Wèi general Páng Juān heard of this,

The Qí army had already passed and was heading west.
Sūnzi said to Tián Jì:
"The soldiers of the Three Jìn are known to be fierce and brave and they look down upon Qí.
Qí is known for its timidity.
A good commander takes advantage of the situation and guides it to their advantage.
The art of war states that,
'Those who rush a hundred *lǐ* for advantage will lose their superior general.
Those who rush fifty *lǐ* for advantage will only have half their army arrive.'
Have the Qí army, upon entering Wèi territory, set up 100,000 stoves.
The next day, set up 50,000 stoves.
And the day after that, set up 30,000 stoves."
Páng Juān traveled for three days,

"I knew the Qí army was timid.
Entering my territory for three days,

Thereupon, he abandoned his infantry

Sūnzǐ estimated their pace,

The road to Mǎlíng was narrow,

"Páng Juān will die under this tree."
Then he ordered ten thousand crossbowmen, the best archers in the Qí army,

"When you see a fire lit at dusk, fire all at once."
Páng Juān indeed arrived at the cut tree at night,

He then lit a torch to illuminate it.
Before he finished reading the message,
the ten thousand crossbows of the Qí army fired all at once,

Páng Juān, realizing that his wisdom was exhausted and his army defeated,

"So I have helped that boy achieve fame!"
Qí then took advantage of their victory to completely destroy the Wèi army,

Sūn Bìn thereby became famous throughout the world,
His military strategies were passed down through the generations.

Now Wú Gōng has again sucked the carbuncle of her son,

Hán.

The world generally praises military strategy,

The world possesses many copies

The saying goes:

Sūnzǐ's strategies were clear to Páng Juān,

Wǔ Zǐxū 伍子胥 persuaded Wú Wáng Liáo 吳王僚, saying:
"Chǔ 楚 can be defeated.
I wish to send Gōngzǐ Guāng 公子光 again."
Gōngzǐ Guāng 公子光 said to Wú Wáng 吳王:
"That Wǔ Xū 伍胥's father and brothers were killed in Chǔ 楚,
and he is urging the king to attack Chǔ 楚,
he only wants to avenge his hatred.
Attacking Chǔ 楚 will not necessarily lead to victory."
Wǔ Xū 伍胥 knew that Gōngzǐ Guāng 公子光 had internal ambitions,
wanting to kill the king and establish himself,
and could not be persuaded with external affairs,
so he introduced Zhuān Zhū 專諸 to Gōngzǐ Guāng 公子光,
and retired to till the fields with the son of Crown Prince Jiàn 建, Shèng 勝.
Five years later, Chǔ Píng Wáng 楚平王 died.
Initially, the Qin 秦 woman whom Píng Wáng 平王 had taken from Crown Prince Jiàn 建 bore a son, Zhěn 軫.
When Píng Wáng 平王 died,
Zhěn 軫 eventually became the successor,
becoming Zhāo Wáng 昭王.
Wú Wáng Liáo 吳王僚, taking advantage of the mourning in Chǔ 楚,
sent two princes to lead troops to attack Chǔ 楚.
Chu sent troops to cut off the Wu troops' retreat,
so they could not return.
The state of Wu was internally empty,
and so Prince Guang then ordered Zhuan Zhu to assassinate King Liao of Wu and establish himself,
he became King Helü of Wu.
Once Helü was established,
having achieved his ambition,
he then summoned Wu Yuan to be a "traveler" (envoy),
and consulted with him on matters of state.
Chu executed its ministers Xi Wan,
Bo Zhou Li,
Bo Zhou Li's grandson Bo Pi fled and sought refuge in Wu,
Wu also made Pi a grand master (minister).
The two princes previously sent by King Liao to lead troops to attack Chu,
were cut off and could not return.
Later, hearing that Helü had assassinated King Liao and established himself,
they then surrendered their troops to Chu,
Chu enfeoffed them at Shu.
Three years after Helü was established,
he then raised an army with Wu Xu,
and Bo Pi to attack Chu,
captured Shu,
and then captured the two former Wu generals who had defected.
Consequently, they wanted to reach Ying,
General Sun Wu said:
"The people are weary,
it is not yet possible,
"Just wait for it."
Thereupon, he returned.
In the fourth year,
Wú 吳 attacked Chǔ 楚,
taking Lù 六 and Qián 灊.
In the fifth year,
they attacked Yuè 越,
defeating them.
In the sixth year,
King Zhāo of Chǔ 楚昭王 sent Gōngzǐ Nángwǎ 公子囊瓦 to lead troops to attack Wú 吳.
Wú 吳 sent Wǔ Yuán 伍員 to meet and attack them,
greatly defeating the Chǔ 楚 army at Yùzhāng 豫章,
taking Jūcháo 居巢 of Chǔ 楚.
In the ninth year,
King Hélǘ of Wú 吳王闔廬 said to Zǐ Xū 子胥 and
Sūn Wǔ 孫武,
"Initially you said Yǐng 郢 could not be entered,
how is it now?"
The two men replied,
"The Chǔ 楚 general Nángwǎ 囊瓦 is greedy,
and Táng 唐 and
Cài 蔡 both resent him.
If the king truly wishes to greatly attack them,
he must first obtain Táng 唐 and
Cài 蔡, then it will be possible."
Hélǘ 闔廬 listened to them,
Xī entirely mobilized his army to attack Chǔ with Táng and Cài.
They arrayed their forces along the Hàn River facing Chǔ.
The younger brother of the King of Wú, Fūgài, led troops and requested to join the campaign.
The King did not listen.
Thereupon, Fūgài led his contingent of 5,000 men to attack the Chǔ general Zǐcháng.
Zǐcháng was defeated and fled,
escaping to Zhèng.
Thereupon, Wú, taking advantage of the victory, advanced forward.
In five battles,
they finally reached Yǐng.
On the day jǐmǎo,
King Zhāo of Chǔ fled.
On the day gēngchén,
the King of Wú entered Yǐng.
King Zhāo fled into exile,
entering the Yúnmèng marshes.
Robbers attacked the King,
and the King fled to Yún.
The younger brother of the Duke of Yún, Huái, said:
"King Píng killed my father.
If I kill his son,
would that not be permissible!"
The Duke of Yún, fearing that his younger brother would kill the King,
fled with the King to Suí.
The Wú army besieged Suí,
saying to the people of Suí:
"The descendants of Zhōu in the Hàn River region,
Chǔ completely annihilated them."
The people of Suí wanted to kill the king,
Prince Qí hid the king,
and declared himself king to take his place.
The people of Suí divined about giving the king to Wú,
but it was inauspicious,
so they declined to give the king to Wú.
Initially, Wǔ Yuán and Shēn Bāoxū were friends,
when Yuán fled,
he said to Bāoxū:
"I will surely overturn Chǔ."
Bāoxū said:
"I will surely preserve it."
When the Wú army entered Yǐng,
Wǔ Zǐxū searched for King Zhāo.
Having not found him,
he dug up the tomb of King Píng of Chǔ,
exhumed his corpse,
and whipped it three hundred times,
then stopped.
Shēn Bāoxū fled into the mountains,
and sent someone to say to Zǐxū:
"Your revenge,
is it not excessive!
I have heard,
that the multitude of people can overcome heaven,
What is determined by Heaven can also be broken by man.
Now, you were originally a minister of King Píng,
personally serving him with the northern-facing position of a subordinate,
but now you have gone so far as to desecrate the dead.
How could this not be the extreme of lacking heavenly principles!"
Wǔ Zǐxū said:
"For me, reply to Shēn Bāoxū,
my sun is setting and my road is long,
so I deliberately act perversely and implement things backwards."
Thereupon, Shēn Bāoxū fled to Qin to urgently report the situation,
seeking aid from Qin.
Qin did not grant it.
Bāoxū stood in the Qin court,
crying day and night,
for seven days and seven nights, his voice did not cease.
Duke Āi of Qin took pity on him,
and said:
"Although Chu is without morality,
having a minister like this,
how could it not be preserved!"
Thereupon, he sent five hundred chariots to rescue Chu and attack Wu.
In the sixth month,
they defeated the Wu troops at Jì.
It happened that the King of Wu had been staying in Chu for a long time seeking King Zhāo,
but Hélǘ's younger brother, Fūgài, fled back home,
and established himself as king.
Hélǘ heard of this,
so he abandoned Chu and returned,
attacking his brother Fūgài.
Fūgài was defeated and fled,
then fled to Chu.
King Zhāo of Chu, seeing that Wu had internal strife,
then re-entered Yǐng.
He enfeoffed Fūgài in Tángxī,
making him the Tángxī clan.
Chǔ again fought with Wú,
defeating Wú,
and the King of Wú then returned.
Two years later,
Hélǘ sent Crown Prince Fūchāi to lead troops to attack Chǔ,
taking Fān.
Chǔ, fearing that Wú would return in great force,
then abandoned Yǐng
and moved to Ruò.
At that time,
Wú, with the strategies of Wǔ Zǐxū
and Sūn Wǔ,
to the west broke the mighty Chǔ,
to the north awed Qí and Jìn,
and to the south subdued the people of Yuè.
Four years later,
Confucius became Chancellor of Lǔ.
Five years later,
An attack on Yuè.
The King of Yuè, Gōu Jiàn, met them in battle,
defeating Wú at Gūsū,
and wounding Hélǘ's finger,
forcing the army to retreat.
Hélǘ, sick from his wound and near death,
said to his heir apparent, Fūchāi:
"Have you forgotten that Gōu Jiàn killed your father?"
Fūchāi replied:
"I dare not forget."
That evening,
Hélǘ died.
Fūchāi, having ascended the throne as king,
appointed Bó Pǐ as Grand Tutor,
and practiced warfare and archery.
Two years later, he attacked Yuè,
defeating Yuè at Fūqiū.
The King of Yuè, Gōu Jiàn, then retreated with the remaining five thousand soldiers to the top of Mount Kuàijī,
and sent the Grand Master Zhǒng with lavish gifts to Wú's Grand Tutor, Pǐ, to sue for peace,
offering to surrender his kingdom and become servants.
The King of Wú was about to agree to it.
Wǔ Zǐxū advised, saying:
"The King of Yuè is capable of enduring hardship.
If you do not destroy him now,
you will surely regret it later."
The King of Wú did not listen,
followed the plan of Grand Tutor Pǐ,
and made peace with Yuè.
Five years later,
the King of Wú heard that Duke Jǐng of Qí had died and his ministers were vying for power,
and that the new ruler was weak.
Thereupon, he raised an army to invade Qí to the north.
Wǔ Zǐxū advised,
"Gōu Jiàn does not eat delicacies twice,
offers condolences at funerals, inquires after the sick,
and moreover, he intends to employ [his people].
If this man does not die,
he will surely become a problem for Wú.
Now, Wú's possession of Yuè
is like a man having a disease in his abdomen and heart.
But Your Majesty does not prioritize Yuè but instead focuses on Qí,
is that not a mistake!"
The King of Wú did not listen,
and attacked Qí,
inflicting a great defeat on the Qí army at Àilíng,
and then intimidated the rulers of Zōu and Lǔ before returning.
He became increasingly distant from Zǐxū's plans.
Four years later,
the King of Wú was about to invade Qí to the north.
King Gōu Jiàn of Yuè, using the plan of Zǐ Gòng,
then led his troops to assist Wú,
and offered valuable treasures as gifts to Tài Zǎi Pǐ.
Tài Zǎi Pǐ, having repeatedly received bribes from Yuè,
loved and trusted Yuè extraordinarily,
Day and night he spoke to the King of Wu.
The King of Wu trusted Pǐ's schemes.
Wǔ Zǐxū remonstrated, saying:
"Now, Yue,
is a disease of the heart and belly,
but now you trust their flattering, deceitful words and are greedy for Qi.
Conquering Qi
is like a stony field,
of no use.
Moreover, the 'Announcement of Pán Gēng' says:
'Those who overturn [the government] and are disrespectful,
cut off their noses and exterminate them,
so that no offspring are left behind,
and do not allow the seed to be changed in this city.'
This is why the Shang dynasty prospered.
I wish that the King would abandon Qi and prioritize Yue;
if not,
later you will regret it, but it will be too late."
But the King of Wu did not listen
and sent Zǐxū to Qi.
As Zǐxū was about to depart,
he said to his son:
"I have repeatedly remonstrated with the King,
but the King does not listen.
Now I foresee the downfall of Wu.
If you perish with Wu,
it will be of no benefit."
Thereupon, he entrusted his son to Bào Mù of Qi,
And then returned to report to Wú.
The Grand Master of Wú, Pǐ, already had a feud with Zǐxū,
and thus slandered him, saying:
"Zǐxū is a person who is stubborn and violent,
with little kindness,
suspicious and treacherous,
his resentment is feared to become a deep calamity.
The other day, the King wanted to attack Qí,
Zǐxū thought it was not permissible,
but the King ultimately attacked it and had great success.
Zǐxū is ashamed that his plans were not used,
and thus resents it.
And now the King again wants to attack Qí,
Zǐxū stubbornly and forcefully remonstrates,
obstructs and undermines affairs,
merely hoping for Wú to fail in order to prove his own plans were correct.
Now the King goes himself,
using all the military force in the state to attack Qí,
but Zǐxū's remonstrances were not accepted,
so he stopped, excused himself,
feigning illness and not going.
The King must be prepared,
it would not be difficult for him to cause trouble.
Moreover, Pǐ sent people to secretly observe him,
when he was sent to Qí,
he entrusted his son to the Bào family of Qí.
Now, as a subject,
Being discontented internally,
relying on the various lords externally,
considering himself a strategist of the former king,
but now not being employed,
he constantly harbored resentment and discontent.
I hope Your Majesty plans for this early."
King of Wú said:
"What Wēi Zǐ said,
I also suspect it."
Thereupon, he sent a messenger to bestow upon Wǔ Zǐxū the Shǔlóu sword,
saying:
"Use this to die."
Wǔ Zǐxū, looking up to the sky, sighed and said:
"Alas!
The slandering minister Pǐ is creating chaos,
and the king is instead punishing me.
I made your father a hegemon.
From the time you were not yet established,
the various nobles contended to be established,
I fought with my life for this with the former king,
and you almost were not established.
After you were established,
you wanted to divide the state of Wú and give it to me,
but I did not dare hope for it.
Yet now you listen to the words of flattering ministers to kill an elder."
Thereupon, he told his retainers:
"Be sure to plant catalpa trees on my grave,
which can now be made into vessels,
and gouge out my eyes and hang them above the east gate of Wú,
so I may watch the Yuè bandits enter and destroy Wú!”
Thereupon, he slit his own throat and died.
The King of Wú, hearing of this, was greatly angered,
and took Zǐxū's corpse, put it in a leather bag of chìyí,
and floated it in the river.
The people of Wú pitied him,
and built a shrine for him on the riverbank,
and named it Mount Xū.
After the King of Wú executed Wǔ Zǐxū,
he then attacked Qí.
The Bào family of Qí killed their lord, Duke Dào, and installed Yáng Shēng.
The King of Wú wanted to punish the rebels,
but was unable to and left.
Two years later,
the King of Wú summoned the lords of Lǔ and Wèi to meet at Tuógāo.
The following year,
he held a grand assembly of the lords north of the Héng Pond,
to command the Zhōu royal house.
King Gōujiàn of Yuè launched a surprise attack, killing the Crown Prince of Wú
and defeating the Wú army.
The King of Wú, hearing of this,
then returned
and sent envoys with generous gifts to make peace with Yuè.
Nine years later,
King Gōujiàn of Yuè finally destroyed Wú,
killing King Fūchāi;
And he executed Tài Zǎi Pǐ,
because he was disloyal to his lord,
and outwardly received heavy bribes,
and formed cliques with others.
Wǔ Zǐxū initially fled together with Shèng, the son of the late Chǔ Crown Prince Jiàn,
who was in Wú.
During the reign of King Fūchāi of Wú,
King Huì of Chǔ wanted to summon Shèng back to Chǔ.
Lord Yè advised, saying:
"Shèng is fond of bravery and secretly seeks out desperadoes,
he probably has private intentions!"
King Huì did not listen.
He then summoned Shèng
and had him reside in Yān, a border town of Chǔ,
with the title Bái Gōng.
Three years after Bái Gōng returned to Chǔ, Wú executed Zǐxū.
After Bái Gōng Shèng returned to Chǔ,
he resented Zhèng for killing his father,
so he secretly nurtured desperadoes to seek revenge on Zhèng.
Five years after returning to Chǔ,
he requested to attack Zhèng,
and the Chǔ chief minister Zǐxī approved it.
Before the army could depart, Jìn attacked Zhèng,
and Zhèng requested aid from Chǔ.
Chǔ sent Zǐxī to provide aid,
and they formed an alliance and returned.
Bái Gōng Shèng 白公勝 angrily said:
"The feud is not with Zhèng 鄭,
but with Zǐxī 子西."
Shèng 勝 sharpened his sword himself.
Someone asked,
"What is it for?"
Shèng 勝 said:
"I want to kill Zǐxī 子西 with it."
Zǐxī 子西 heard of this
and laughed, saying:
"Shèng 勝 is like an egg;
what can he do?"
Four years later,
Bái Gōng Shèng 白公勝 and Shí Qǐ 石乞 ambushed and killed the Chief Minister of Chǔ 楚, Zǐxī 子西, and the Minister of War, Zǐqí 子綦, in the court.
the Sīmǎ 司馬 Zǐ Qí 子綦 at court.
Shí Qǐ 石乞 said:
"Not killing the King
is not acceptable."
He then kidnapped the King to Gāo 高 Palace.
Shí Qǐ's 石乞 follower, Qū Gù 屈固, carried King Huì of Chǔ 楚 on his back and fled to the palace of Lady Zhāo 昭.
Yè Gōng 葉公 heard that Bái Gōng 白公 had caused a rebellion
and led the people of his state to attack Bái Gōng 白公.
Bái Gōng's 白公 followers were defeated.
He fled into the mountains
and committed suicide.
They captured Shí Qǐ 石乞,
and asked where Bái Gōng's 白公 corpse was,
He did not speak, and was about to be boiled.
Shí Qǐ said:
"If the affair succeeds, I become a minister,
if it fails, I am boiled.
It is certainly my duty."
He ultimately refused to reveal where the corpse was located.
Consequently, they boiled Shí Qǐ,
and asked King Huì to reinstate him.
The Grand Scribe said:
The bitterness of resentment is truly extreme for people!
Even a king cannot inflict it upon his subjects,
let alone those of equal rank!
If Wǔ Zǐxū had followed Shē to his death,
how would it be different from ants?
Abandoning small righteousness,
wiping away great shame,
his name is passed down to later generations,
how sad!
When Zǐxū was in straits on the riverbank,
begging for food on the road,
could his determination have ever momentarily forgotten Yǐng?
Therefore, enduring hardship to achieve fame and merit,
if not a heroic man, who could accomplish this?
If Bái Gōng had not set himself up as ruler,
his accomplishments and schemes would also be unspeakable!
"Biographies of the Disciples of Zhòng Ní, Seven"
Confucius said,
"Those who received instruction and became proficient numbered seventy-seven,"
all of them men of exceptional ability.
In Virtue:
Yán Yuān,
Mǐn Zǐqiān,
Rǎn Bóniú,
Zhòng Gōng.
In Government Affairs:
Rǎn Yǒu,
Jì Lù.
In Eloquence:
Zǎi Wǒ,
Zǐ Gòng.
In Literature:
Zǐ Yóu,
Zǐ Xià.
Shī was biased,
Cān was slow,
Chái was dull,
Yóu was coarse,
Huí was frequently empty [of provisions].
Cì did not accept [Heaven's] mandate, and engaged in accumulating wealth,
and in his speculations, he was frequently correct.
Those whom Confucius treated with great respect:
in Zhou, Lǎozi;
In Wèi,
Qū Bóyù;
in Qí,
Yàn Píngzhòng;
in Chǔ,
Lǎo Lái Zi;
in Zhèng,
Zǐchǎn;
in Lǔ,
Mèng Gōngchuò.
When repeatedly mentioning Zāng Wénzhòng,
Liǔxià Huì,
Tóngdī Bó Huá,
Jiè Shān Zǐrán,
Kǒngzǐ always ranked them after himself,
not as contemporaries.
Yán Huí,
was a person from Lǔ,
his style name was Zǐyuān.
He was thirty years younger than Kǒngzǐ.
Yán Yuān asked about benevolence,
Kǒngzǐ said:
"To subdue oneself and return to propriety is benevolence.
All under Heaven will return to benevolence."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"How virtuous is Huí!
A bamboo container of food,
a gourd of drink,
living in a humble lane,
others cannot endure such hardship,
but Huí does not change his joy."
"Huí is like a fool;
but after I withdraw and examine his private conduct,
I find that he is perfectly capable of understanding,
Huí (回) is not foolish."
"When employed, he acts;
when dismissed, he retires;
only I and you have this quality!"
Huí (回) was twenty-nine years old,
his hair was completely white,
and he died young.
Kǒngzǐ (孔子) mourned him bitterly,
saying:
"Since I had Huí (回),
the disciples have become more intimate."
Lǔ Āi Gōng (魯哀公) asked:
"Which of your disciples is considered diligent in learning?"
Kǒngzǐ (孔子) replied:
"There was Yán Huí (顏回) who was diligent in learning,
he did not transfer his anger to others,
and he did not repeat his mistakes.
Unfortunately, he died young,
now he is gone."
Mǐn Sǔn, zì Zǐqiān.
(He was) fifteen years younger than Kǒngzǐ.
Kǒngzǐ said:
"How filial is Mǐn Zǐqiān!
People can find no fault with his parents and elder brothers' words (about him)."
He did not serve any grandee,
nor did he accept the salary of a corrupt ruler.
(He said,) "If anyone seeks me out again,
(they will) surely (find me) on the banks of the Wèn River."
Rǎn Gēng, zì Bóniú.
Kǒngzǐ considered him to have virtue.
Bóniú had a terrible disease.
Kǒngzǐ went to inquire after him.
From the window, he grasped his hand,
and said:
"It is fate!
That such a person should have such a disease,
it is fate!"
Rǎn Yōng, zì Zhònggōng.
Zhònggōng asked about government.
Kǒngzǐ said:
"When going out the door, (behave) as if you are receiving a great guest;
He made the people feel as if they were participating in a great sacrifice.
There was no resentment in the state,
and no resentment in the family."
Confucius considered Zhònggōng to be a man of virtue,
and said:
"Yōng could be made to face south."
Zhònggōng's father was
a man of low status.
Confucius said:
"If the calf of a brindled ox is red and has horns,
even if one wishes not to use it,
would the mountains and rivers reject it?"
Rǎn Qiú, styled Zǐyǒu,
was twenty-nine years younger than Confucius.
He became the steward of the Jì family.
Jì Kāngzǐ asked Confucius, saying:
"Is Rǎn Qiú benevolent?"
He replied:
"In a town of a thousand households,
or a family with a hundred chariots,
Qiú could be employed to govern its taxes.
As for benevolence, I do not know."
He asked again:
"Is Zǐlù benevolent?"
Confucius answered,
"Like Qiú."
Qiú asked,
"Should I act immediately upon hearing something?"
Confucius said,
"Act on it."
Zǐlù asked,
"Should I act immediately upon hearing something?"
Confucius said,
"With your father and elder brothers still living,
how could you act immediately upon hearing something!"
Zǐ Huá found it strange,
"May I ask, the questions were the same, but the answers were different?"
Confucius said,
"Qiú is timid,
therefore I encourage him.
Yóu is overzealous,
therefore I restrain him."
Zhòng Yóu, styled Zǐlù,
was a man of Biàn.
He was nine years younger than Confucius.
Zǐlù's nature was crude,
he loved bravery and strength,
his will was defiant and direct,
he wore a rooster's crown,
(He) wore a boar's and piglet's hide,
and rudely insulted Confucius (Kǒngzǐ).
Confucius (Kǒngzǐ) established rites and gradually enticed Zǐlù,
Zǐlù later donned scholar's robes and submitted himself,
and through the disciples of Confucius (Kǒngzǐ), requested to become a disciple.
Zǐlù asked about governance.
Confucius (Kǒngzǐ) said:
"Lead them,
and toil for them."
(Zǐlù) requested more instruction.
(Confucius (Kǒngzǐ)) said:
"Do not weary."
Zǐlù asked:
"Does the junzi (君子, gentleman) value courage?"
Confucius (Kǒngzǐ) said:
"Righteousness is paramount.
If a junzi (君子, gentleman) loves courage but lacks righteousness, there will be chaos;
if a petty person loves courage but lacks righteousness, there will be thievery."
When Zǐlù heard something,
he had not yet put it into practice,
but he feared hearing something new.
Confucius (Kǒngzǐ) said:
"The one who can settle a lawsuit with a single phrase,
it is probably Yóu!"
"Yóu is more courageous than I am,
but he doesn't know how to adapt."
"If it's Yóu,
he won't die a natural death."
"To wear a tattered hemp gown and stand without shame alongside those wearing fox and badger furs,
that's Yóu!"
"Yóu has ascended to the hall,
but he has not yet entered the inner chamber."
Jì Kāngzǐ asked:
"Is Zhòng Yóu benevolent?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"In a state with a thousand chariots, he could be employed to manage its taxes,
but I don't know about his benevolence."
Zǐlù enjoyed following him on his travels,
and encountered Cháng Jǔ,
Jié Nì,
and an old man carrying a hoe.
Zǐlù became steward for the Jì family,
and Jì Sūn asked,
"Can Zǐlù be called a great minister?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"He can be called a capable minister."
Zǐlù became the magistrate of Pú,
and took his leave of Kǒngzǐ.
Confucius said:
"In Pu there are many brave men,
and they are difficult to govern.
However, I tell you:
with respect and reverence,
one can control bravery;
with generosity and righteousness,
one can unite the masses;
with respect, righteousness, and tranquility,
one can repay one's superiors."
Initially,
Duke Ling of Wei had a favored concubine named Nánzǐ.
Crown Prince Kuì Kuì offended Nánzǐ,
feared punishment, and fled.
When Duke Ling died, the (chief) wife wanted to establish Prince Yǐng.
Yǐng was unwilling,
saying:
"The son of the exiled Crown Prince, Zhé, is here."
Thereupon, Wei established Zhé as the ruler,
and he became known as Duke Chū.
Duke Chū reigned for twelve years,
while his father, Kuì Kuì, remained outside (the country),
unable to enter.
Zǐlù was the magistrate of the town of Kǒng Kuī, a high official of Wei.
Kuì Kuì then conspired with Kǒng Kuī to create turmoil,
planning to enter the Kǒng Kuī household,
and consequently, with his followers, attacked Duke Chū.
Chū Gōng fled to Lǔ,
and Kuì Kuì entered and established himself,
and was known as Zhuāng Gōng.
When Kǒng Kuī caused a rebellion,
Zǐ Lù was away,
but upon hearing of it, he rode swiftly back.
He encountered Zǐ Gāo exiting the city gate of Wèi,
who said to Zǐ Lù:
"Chū Gōng has left,
and the gate is already closed.
You should return,
and not suffer misfortune in vain."
Zǐ Lù said:
"One who eats their food does not shirk their difficulties."
Zǐ Gāo eventually left.
A messenger entered the city,
the city gate opened,
and Zǐ Lù followed and entered.
He went to see Kuì Kuì,
who was ascending the platform with Kǒng Kuī.
Zǐ Lù said:
"Why does Your Lordship need Kǒng Kuī?
Allow me to kill him."
Kuì Kuì did not listen.
Thereupon, Zǐ Lù wanted to burn the platform.
Kuì Kuì was afraid,
and sent Shí Qǐ
and Hú Yǎn to attack Zǐ Lù,
He struck and broke Zǐlù's ǎ (Hànyǔ Pīnyīn: Zǐlù) hat string.
Zǐlù (Hànyǔ Pīnyīn: Zǐlù) said:
"A gentleman dies, but his hat is not removed."
Thereupon, he tied his hat string and died.
Kǒngzǐ (Hànyǔ Pīnyīn: Kǒngzǐ) heard of the unrest in Wèi (Hànyǔ Pīnyīn: Wèi),
and said:
"Alas,
Yóu (Hànyǔ Pīnyīn: Yóu) is dead!"
Soon after, he indeed died.
Therefore, Kǒngzǐ (Hànyǔ Pīnyīn: Kǒngzǐ) said:
"Since I obtained Yóu (Hànyǔ Pīnyīn: Yóu),
evil words have not been heard in my ears."
At this time, Zǐgòng (Hànyǔ Pīnyīn: Zǐgòng) was serving as an envoy from Lǔ (Hànyǔ Pīnyīn: Lǔ) to Qí (Hànyǔ Pīnyīn: Qí).
Zǎiyǔ (Hànyǔ Pīnyīn: Zǎiyǔ)'s courtesy name was Zǐwǒ (Hànyǔ Pīnyīn: Zǐwǒ).
He was eloquent and skilled in debate.
After receiving instruction,
he asked:
"Is a three-year mourning period not too long?
If a gentleman does not practice ritual for three years,
ritual will surely decay;
if he does not practice music for three years,
music will surely collapse.
The old grain is already exhausted,
and the new grain has already risen;
the fire-drills have been changed,
the period may be ended."
The Master said:
"Are you at peace with it?"
He replied:
"I am at peace."
"If you are at peace with it, then do it.
When a gentleman is in mourning,
eating delicacies is not sweet,
hearing music is not joyful,
therefore he does not do it."
Zǎi Wǒ withdrew,
the Master said:
"Yǔ is inhumane!
A child is only free from his parents' embrace after three years.
Now, the three years of mourning
is a universal principle under Heaven."
Zǎi Yǔ slept during the daytime.
The Master said:
"Rotten wood cannot be carved,
a wall of dung cannot be troweled."
Zǎi Wǒ asked about the virtue of the Five Emperors,
the Master said:
"I am not the right person."
Zǎi Wǒ became a grand master of Línzī,
and rebelled with Tián Cháng,
leading to the extermination of his clan,
Confucius was ashamed of it.
Duānmù Cì,
was a person from Wèi,
his courtesy name was Zǐgòng.
He was thirty-one years younger than Confucius.
Zǐgòng was skilled in speech and clever in words,
Confucius often rejected his arguments.
He asked,
"Who is better, you or Huí?"
He replied,
"How would Cì dare to compare to Huí!
Huí hears one thing and understands ten,
Cì hears one thing and understands two."
After Zǐgòng had already received instruction,
he asked,
"What kind of person is Cì?"
Confucius said,
"You are a vessel."
He asked,
"What kind of vessel?"
He said,
"A húlián sacrificial vessel."
Chén Zǐqín asked Zǐgòng,
"From whom did Zhòngní learn?"
Zǐ Gòng said:
"The Way of Wén and Wǔ has not fallen to the ground;
it is in people.
The wise recognize the greater aspects of it;
the unwise recognize the lesser aspects of it;
none are without the Way of Wén and Wǔ.
What is there that the Master does not learn?
And yet why would he have a constant teacher!"
He asked again, saying:
"When Kǒngzǐ goes to a state, he invariably hears about its government.
Does he seek it out?
Or is it given to him?"
Zǐ Gòng said:
"The Master obtains it through being gentle, kind, respectful, thrifty, and yielding.
The Master's seeking it,
is surely different from others' seeking it."
Zǐ Gòng asked, saying:
"To be rich without being arrogant,
and poor without being obsequious,
what do you think of this?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"That is acceptable;
but it is not as good as being poor and delighting in the Way,
and rich and loving ritual propriety."
Tián Cháng desired to create rebellion in Qí,
and feared Gāo,
Guó, Bào,
Yàn, therefore moved their troops intending to attack Lǔ.
Kǒngzǐ heard of it,
and said to his disciples:
"Lǔ,
is where our ancestors' graves are located,
it is the country of our parents,
the country is in such danger,
why do none of you come forward?"
Zǐlù requested to go,
Kǒngzǐ stopped him.
Zǐzhāng,
Zǐshí requested to go,
Kǒngzǐ did not permit them.
Zǐgòng requested to go,
Kǒngzǐ permitted him.
Thereupon he departed,
arrived in Qí,
and persuaded Tián Cháng, saying:
"Your lord's attack on Lǔ is a mistake.
For Lǔ,
is a difficult country to attack,
its walls are thin and low,
its land is narrow and exposed,
its ruler is foolish and unkind,
its ministers are deceitful and useless,
and its soldiers and people detest the matters of armor and weapons,
this country cannot be fought against.
Your lord is better off attacking Wú.
For Wú,
its walls are high and thick,
its land is broad and deep,
its armor is sturdy and new,
its soldiers selected and well-fed,
important weapons and elite troops are all within,
and you would have a wise minister guarding it,
this is easy to attack."
Tián Cháng angrily changed his expression and said:
"What you consider difficult,
others consider easy;
what you consider easy,
others consider difficult.
And you use this to instruct Cháng,
why?"
Zǐ Gòng said:
"Your servant has heard it said,
those who have internal worries attack the strong,
those who have external worries attack the weak.
Now, lord, you have internal worries.
I have heard that you were enfeoffed three times and each time it failed,
that your ministers did not listen.
Now you destroy Lǔ to expand Qí,
you use victory to make the ruler arrogant,
you destroy countries to honor your ministers,
and your merits are not counted towards the ruler,
then his relationship with the ruler will daily become more distant.
This is because the lord is arrogant and disregards the ruler's heart,
and below he indulges his ministers.
To seek to accomplish great deeds with this,
is difficult.
For if the lord is arrogant, he will be indulgent,
and if the ministers are arrogant, they will contend.
This means that the lord has disagreements with the ruler above,
and below he is in contention with the great ministers.
If this is the case,
then the lord's position in Qí is perilous.
Therefore it is said that it is better to attack Wú.
If attacking Wú is not successful,
the common people will die abroad,
and the great ministers will be depleted internally.
This means that the lord above will have no strong ministerial enemies,
and below there will be no faults of the common people.
The one who can control Qí as a lone ruler will be the lord."
Tián Cháng said:
"Good.
Although,
my troops have already been deployed against Lǔ,
to withdraw and go to Wú,
the great ministers will suspect me,
what should be done?"
Zǐ Gòng said:
"Your Lordship should hold back the troops and not attack.
I request to go and be an envoy to the King of Wú,
Order him to rescue Lu and attack Qi,
and your lord can then use troops to welcome him."
Tián Cháng agreed to this
and sent Zǐ Gòng south to see the King of Wu.
He argued, saying:
"I have heard that
a true king does not cut off the lineage of states,
and a hegemon has no powerful enemies,
a weight of a thousand jun can be moved by adding only a zhu and a liang.
Now, to use the state of Qi with ten thousand chariots to privately assist the state of Lu with a thousand chariots
is to compete with Wu for strength,
and I privately consider this dangerous for Your Majesty.
Moreover, rescuing Lu
brings fame;
attacking Qi
brings great benefit.
It can pacify the lords of the area around the Si River,
punish the tyrannical Qi, and subdue the powerful Jin;
there is no greater benefit than this.
To nominally preserve the endangered Lu
is in reality to weaken the powerful Qi,
and a wise person would not hesitate in this."
The King of Wu said:
"Good.
However,
I once fought with Yue
and was besieged in Kuaiji.
Yuè Wáng 越王 (King of Yue) endured hardships to nurture his officers,
hoping that they would repay my kindness.
I will consider your request after I attack Yue."
Zǐ Gòng 子貢 said,
"The strength of Yue does not surpass that of Lu,
and the power of Wu does not exceed that of Qi.
If Your Majesty sets aside Qi and attacks Yue,
then Qi will have already conquered Lu.
Moreover, Your Majesty is now establishing a reputation for preserving the fallen and continuing the extinct.
To attack the small state of Yue while fearing the powerful state of Qi
is not courageous.
The courageous do not avoid difficulties,
the benevolent do not abandon the impoverished,
the wise do not miss opportunities,
and the true king does not allow his lineage to be cut off,
in order to establish his righteousness.
Now, preserving Yue will demonstrate benevolence to the other lords.
Saving Lu and attacking Qi
will add prestige to the state of Jin.
The feudal lords will certainly follow each other in paying court to Wu,
and hegemony will be achieved.
Furthermore, Your Majesty surely despises Yue.
Allow me to travel east to see the King of Yue
and have him send troops to follow you.
This will actually empty Yue,
while nominally following the feudal lords in attacking (Qi)."
The King of Wu was greatly pleased
and sent Zǐ Gòng 子貢 to Yue.
The King of Yue cleared the roads and greeted him in the suburbs,
personally driving the chariot to his residence and asking,
"This is a barbarian country.
Why does the esteemed sir condescend to honor it with his presence?"
Zǐ Gòng 子貢 said:
"Now, I persuaded the King of Wú to save Lǔ by attacking Qí.
He desired it in his heart but feared Yuè,
saying,
'Only after I attack Yuè will it be possible.'
In this way,
the defeat of Yuè is assured.
Moreover, to have no intention of revenge but cause others to suspect it is foolish;
that is clumsy.
To have the intention of revenge
but let others know it is perilous;
that is dangerous.
For a matter to be heard of before it has even begun
is precarious;
that is perilous. These three are the great calamities in undertaking an affair."
Gōujiàn kowtowed twice and said,
"I once misjudged my strength
and fought with Wú,
and was trapped at Kuàijī.
The pain penetrates to my bones.
Day and night, my lips and tongue are parched,
and I merely wish to die heel-to-toe with the King of Wú.
That is my desire."
Thereupon he asked Zǐgòng.
Zǐgòng said:
"The King of Wú is fierce and violent by nature,
his ministers cannot endure him;
the state is exhausted from repeated wars,
the soldiers cannot bear it;
the common people resent their ruler,
great ministers plot internal rebellion;
Zǐxū died for his admonitions,
the Grand Tutor Pǐ is in power,
he indulges the ruler's faults to secure his own private interests:
this is the way to ruin a state.
Now, if Your Majesty sincerely sends soldiers to assist him in achieving his ambition,
uses lavish treasures to please his heart,
and humble words to honor his etiquette,
then he will surely attack Qí.
If he fights and is not victorious,
it will be a blessing for Your Majesty.
If he wins the battle,
he will certainly use his army to threaten Jìn.
I ask to go north and meet with the ruler of Jìn,
to have them attack him together,
weakening Wú is certain.
His elite troops will be exhausted in Qí,
his heavily armored soldiers will be worn down in Jìn,
and Your Majesty can control his exhaustion,
in this way, destroying Wú is certain."
The King of Yuè was very pleased,
and agreed to it.
He gifted Zǐgòng one hundred yì of gold,
one sword,
and two fine spears.
Zǐgòng did not accept them,
and then departed.
He reported to the King of Wú, saying:
"Your subject respectfully conveyed Your Majesty's words to the King of Yuè,
and the King of Yuè was greatly afraid,
saying:
'I am unfortunate,
having lost my ancestors early,
and not knowing my own limitations,
I offended Wú,
my army was defeated, and my person was disgraced,
and I dwelt in Kuài Jī,
my country became desolate and overgrown,
but relying on Your Majesty's grace,
I was able to offer sacrifices and continue ancestral rites,
which I dare not forget even in death,
what schemes would I dare to consider!'"
Five days later,
the Yuè envoy, Dà Fū Zhǒng, kowtowed and said to the King of Wú:
"Your subject Zhǒng, a servant from the Eastern Sea and an envoy of the lonely Gū Jiàn,
dares to humbly inquire of your attendants.
Now, I have heard that Your Majesty intends to raise a great righteous cause,
punishing the strong and rescuing the weak,
He was troubled by the violent Qí and sought to support the Zhōu royal house.
He requested to mobilize all three thousand soldiers within his territory.
"I, your subject, will personally don armor and bear arms,
to be the first to receive arrows and stones."
Furthermore, he sent his humble subject, Zhǒng Fèng, to present the ancestral armory,
twenty suits of armor,
axes, Qūlú's spears,
and Bù Guāng's swords,
to congratulate the army officers."
The King of Wú was greatly pleased
and told Zǐ Gòng,
"The King of Yuè wants to personally follow me in attacking Qí,
is that acceptable?"
Zǐ Gòng said,
"No.
To empty a man's country,
to take all his people,
and to have his ruler follow,
is unrighteous.
You should accept his gifts,
allow his troops,
but refuse his ruler."
The King of Wú agreed
and then thanked the King of Yuè.
Thereupon, the King of Wú then proceeded to dispatch troops from nine commanderies to attack Qí.
Zǐ Gòng then went to Jìn,
and said to the ruler of Jìn:
"Your subject has heard that
plans not determined in advance cannot cope with sudden emergencies,
troops not prepared beforehand cannot defeat the enemy.
Now, if Qí and Wú are about to fight,
if they fight and do not win,
Yuè will surely cause disorder;
if they fight with Qí and win,
they will surely use their troops to approach Jìn."
The ruler of Jìn was greatly afraid and
said:
"What should be done about this?"
Zǐ Gòng said:
"Prepare your troops and rest your soldiers to await them."
The ruler of Jìn agreed to this.
Zǐ Gòng left and went to Lǔ.
The King of Wú indeed fought with the people of Qí at Ài Líng,
greatly defeating the Qí army,
capturing the troops of seven generals and not returning,
and indeed approached Jìn with troops,
meeting the people of Jìn above Huáng Chí.
Wú and Jìn contended for strength.
The people of Jìn attacked them,
greatly defeating the Wú army.
The King of Yuè heard of this,
crossed the river to attack Wú,
and encamped seven *lǐ* from the city.
The King of Wú heard of this,
He went to Jin and returned,
and fought with Yue at the Five Lakes.
After three battles without victory,
the city gates could not be defended.
Yue then besieged the royal palace,
killed Fūchāi and executed his minister.
After destroying Wu in three years,
they turned eastward and became hegemon.
Therefore, with one journey by Zǐgòng,
Lu was preserved,
Qi was thrown into chaos,
Wu was destroyed,
Jin was strengthened, and Yue became hegemon.
With one diplomatic mission by Zǐgòng,
he caused the powers to destroy each other.
Within ten years,
each of the five states underwent changes.
Zǐgòng liked to depose and promote,
and he shifted his merchandise and wealth according to the times.
He liked to praise the merits of others,
but could not conceal their faults.
He frequently served as minister for Lu and Wei.
His family accumulated thousands of gold coins.
He eventually died in Qi.
Yán Yǎn,
A man from Wú,
with the courtesy name Zǐ Yóu.
He was 45 years younger than Confucius.
After Zǐ Yóu had received instruction,
he became the magistrate of Wǔchéng.
Confucius passed by
and heard the sound of stringed instruments and singing.
Confucius smiled faintly and said,
"Why use an ox-cleaver to kill a chicken?"
Zǐ Yóu said,
"In the past, Yǎn heard from you, Master,
that when a gentleman learns the Dao, he will love people;
when a small man learns the Dao, he is easy to employ."
Confucius said,
"My disciples,
what Yǎn says is right.
My previous words were just a jest."
Confucius considered Zǐ Yóu to be well-versed in literature.
Bǔ Shāng, with the courtesy name Zǐ Xià.
He was 44 years younger than Confucius.
Zǐ Xià asked:
"'Her charming smile is enticing,
Her beautiful eyes are clear,
White silk makes her colorful,'
what does this mean?"
Confucius said:
"Painting comes after the plain white background."
He said:
"Does ritual come after?"
Confucius said:
"Shāng shǐ kě yǔ yán 《Shī》 yǐ yǐ." "Only now can I begin to discuss the *Classic of Poetry* with Shāng."
Zǐgòng wèn: Zǐgòng asked:
"Shī yǔ Shāng shú xián?" "Who is more worthy, Shī or Shāng?"
Zǐ yuē: The Master said:
"Shī yě guò, "Shī goes too far,
Shāng yě bù jí." Shāng does not go far enough."
"Ránzé Shī yù yǔ?" "Then Shī is superior?"
Yuē: The Master said:
"Guò yóu bù jí." "To go too far is the same as not going far enough."
Zǐ wèi Zǐxià yuē: The Master said to Zǐxià:
"Rǔ wèi jūnzǐ rú, "You should be a gentlemanly scholar,
wú wèi xiǎorén rú." do not be a petty scholar."
Kǒngzǐ jì méi, After Kǒngzǐ had passed away,
Zǐxià jū Xīhé jiàoshòu, Zǐxià resided in Xīhé and taught,
wèi Wèi Wénhóu shī. becoming the teacher of Marquis Wén of Wèi.
Qí zǐ sǐ, When his son died,
kū zhī shī míng. he wept for him so excessively that he lost his sight.
Zhuān-sūn Shī, Zhuān-sūn Shī,
Chén Rén,
courtesy name Zǐ Zhāng.
He was forty-eight years younger than Confucius.
Zǐ Zhāng asked about seeking office and its rewards.
Confucius said:
"Listen to much and put aside what you doubt;
cautiously speak about the rest,
then you will have few causes for blame.
See much and put aside what is perilous;
cautiously act on the rest,
then you will have few causes for regret.
When your words give little cause for blame,
and your actions give little cause for regret,
rewards are to be found within that."
Another day, following him between Chén and Cài,
in straits, he asked about conduct.
Confucius said:
"If your words are loyal and trustworthy,
and your actions are sincere and respectful,
you can go anywhere, even in the countries of barbarians.
If your words are not loyal and trustworthy,
and your actions are not sincere and respectful,
how can you go anywhere, even in your own village!
When you stand, see them (loyalty and sincerity) arrayed before you;
when you are in a carriage, see them leaning on the yoke.
Only then can you proceed."
Zǐ Zhāng wrote this on his sash.
Zǐ Zhāng asked,
"What must a scholar be like to be called 'accomplished'?"
Confucius said,
"What is it,
this 'accomplished' you speak of?"
Zǐ Zhāng replied,
"He must be known in the state,
he must be known in his family."
Confucius said,
"That is 'being known,'
not 'accomplishment.'
Now, the 'accomplished' man,
is of genuine uprightness and loves righteousness,
observes words and watches facial expressions,
is considerate and humble toward others;
he is certain to be successful in the state and in his family.
Now, the one who is 'known,'
outwardly assumes benevolence but acts contrary to it,
dwells in it without suspicion;
he is certain to be known in the state and in his family."
Zēng Shēn,
a man from Nán Wǔchéng,
styled Zǐ Yú.
He was forty-six years younger than Confucius.
Confucius considered him capable of understanding the Dao of filial piety,
therefore he imparted knowledge to him.
He composed the *Classic of Filial Piety*.
He died in Lu.
Tántái Mièmíng,
a man of Wǔchéng,
styled Zǐyǔ.
He was thirty-nine years younger than Confucius.
His appearance was very ugly.
He desired to serve Confucius,
Confucius thought his talent was thin.
Once he had received instruction,
he withdrew and cultivated himself,
not taking shortcuts in his conduct,
not meeting with high officials unless it was a public matter.
He traveled south to the Jiang River,
followed by three hundred disciples,
establishing principles of taking and giving, accepting and rejecting,
his reputation was spread among the feudal lords.
Confucius heard of this
and said:
"I judge people by their words,
and I was wrong about Zǎi Yǔ;
I judge people by their appearance,
and I was wrong about Zǐyǔ."
Mì Bùqí, courtesy name Zǐjiàn,
was thirty years younger than Kǒngzǐ.
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Zǐjiàn is a jūnzi!
If Lǔ had no jūnzi,
from where would he have acquired this?"
Zǐjiàn served as the magistrate of Shànfù.
Reporting back to Kǒngzǐ,
he said:
"This state has five worthy men who are not my equals,
who instructed me on how to govern."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"It is a pity that what Bùqí governs is small;
if what he governed were large, it would be almost perfect."
Yuán Xiàn, courtesy name Zǐsī.
Zǐsī asked about shame.
Kǒngzǐ said:
"When the state is governed by the Dao, to receive a salary is proper. When the state is not governed by the Dao, to receive a salary is shameful."
Zǐsī said:
"To suppress boasting, aggression, resentment, and greed,
可以為仁乎？ 」 Kěyǐ wéi rén hū?" "Is it possible to become benevolent?"

公冶長， Gōngyě Cháng, Gōngyě Cháng,
齊人， Qí rén, was a man from Qí,
His courtesy name was Zǐcháng.
Confucius said:
"Cháng is marriageable,
even though he is in shackles,
it is not his fault."
He gave his daughter to him in marriage.
Nángōng Kuò, his courtesy name was Zǐróng.
He asked Confucius, saying:
"Yì was good at archery,
Ào was able to move boats quickly,
yet neither died a natural death;

Lord Shang was

The king remained silent.

After Huì Wáng left,

He appointed Wèi Yāng as Left Chief Administrator
and finally established the laws of reform.
He ordered the people to be organized into groups of ten and five,
mutually supervising and holding each other accountable.
Those who did not report wrongdoers would be cut in half at the waist;
those who reported wrongdoers
would receive the same reward as those who beheaded an enemy soldier;
those who concealed wrongdoers
would be punished the same as those who surrendered to the enemy.
If a family had two or more sons
and did not divide their households,
their taxes would be doubled.
Those who had military merit
would each receive higher ranks according to their achievements;
those who engaged in private fights
would each be punished according to the severity of their actions.
Those who exerted themselves in essential occupations,
such as farming and weaving,
and produced abundant grain and silk
would be exempt from corvée labor.
Those who engaged in petty commerce, as well as the lazy and poor,
were taken as slaves.
Members of the royal family who did not have military merit were not to be included in the register of nobility.
bùdé wéi shǔjí.
He made clear the distinctions of rank
noble rank and hierarchical levels,

Those with merit were displayed in glory,
those without merit,

Once the orders were complete,
but not yet promulgated,
fearing that the people would not believe them,
he then set up a three-zhang-tall pole

The people found this strange,

He announced again:

Finally, he issued the orders.
The orders were implemented among the people for a full year,
The people of Qin in the capital spoke of the inconvenience of the initial decrees by the thousands.
Thereupon, the heir apparent (太子 tàizǐ) violated the law.
Wèi Yāng said:
"The law is not practiced

He was about to apply the law to the heir apparent.
The heir apparent is the successor of the ruler,

The next day,
the people of Qin all hastened to obey the decrees.
After practicing it for ten years,
the people of Qin were greatly pleased.
No one picked up lost articles on the road,
there were no bandits in the mountains,
every household was provided for and the people were content.
The people were brave in public battles,

The villages were greatly governed.
Among the people of Qin who initially said the decrees were inconvenient,

Wèi Yāng said,

He standardized the *dǒu*, *tǒng*, weights, measures, and rulers.

After five years,

The following year,
Wèi Yāng 衛鞅 persuaded Xiào Gōng 孝公, saying:

Furthermore, Wèi 魏 suffered a great defeat at the hands of Qí 齊 last year,

We can take advantage of this opportunity to attack Wèi 魏.
If Wèi 魏 cannot withstand Qín 秦,
it will inevitably move eastward.
If it moves eastward,
Qín 秦, relying on the strength of the Héshān 河山 region,
can face east and control the feudal lords.
This is the foundation of imperial dominion."
Xiào Gōng 孝公 thought this was right

Wèi 魏 sent Gōngzǐ Áng 公子卬 to lead an army to resist him.
Once the armies were facing each other,
Wèi Yāng 衛鞅 sent a letter to the Wèi 魏 general Gōngzǐ Áng 公子卬, saying:
Wèi Yāng sent a letter to the Wei general, Gōngzǐ Áng, saying:

The Wei lord, Gōngzǐ Áng, thought this was reasonable.
After the alliance was formed and they were drinking,

He then attacked his army
and completely defeated it, returning to Qin.
King Huì of Wei's army
was repeatedly defeated by Qi and Qin.
The country was depleted,
and declined daily.
Frightened,
he then sent an envoy to cede the land west of the river
to Qin

King Huì of Liáng said:

After Wèi Yāng returned, having defeated Wei,

Shāng Jūn was the prime minister of Qín for ten years,

Zhào Liáng met with Shāng Jūn.
Shāng Jūn said:

Zhào Liáng said:
"I dare not wish for that.
Kǒng Qiū had a saying:
'Those who promote the virtuous and uphold them advance,

I am unworthy,
therefore I dare not accept your order.
I have heard it said: 'To occupy a position one is not suited for
is called greed for position,
to possess a reputation one does not deserve
is called greed for reputation.'
If I listen to your proposition,
then I fear I would be greedy for position and greedy for reputation.
Therefore, I dare not hear your command."
Shāng Jūn said:
"Do you not approve of my governing of Qín?"
Zhào Liáng said:
"Listening inwardly is called being perceptive,
looking inwardly is called being insightful,
To conquer oneself is called strength.
Yú Shùn had a saying:
'Humble oneself; that is esteemed.'
You would do well to follow the way of Yú Shùn,
and you would have no reason to question me."
Shāng Jūn said:
"Originally, the teachings of the Qín barbarians and Dí
did not distinguish between father and son;
they lived together in the same room.
Now I have changed their teachings
and created distinctions between men and women.
I have greatly built Jì gates,
and the settlements are like those of Lǔ and Wèi.
You have seen how I govern Qín;
who is more virtuous, me or the Grandee of Five Rams?"
Zhào Liáng said:
"The hides of a thousand sheep
are not as good as the fur of one fox;
the yes-men of a thousand people
are not as good as the outspokenness of one scholar.
King Wǔ prospered through outspokenness;
Yīn Zhòu perished through silence.
If you do not disapprove of King Wǔ,
then may I be permitted to speak truthfully all day long
without being punished, is that acceptable?"
Shāng Jūn said:
"There is a saying:
'Elegant words are flowery;
Sincere words are truthful,
bitter words are medicine,
sweet words are sickness.
If you, Master, would truly always speak directly and honestly,
it would be medicine for Yāng.
Yāng will serve you;
what further excuse could you have?"
Zhào Liáng said:
"That Wǔ Gǔ Dàfū (literally, 'Five Ram Minister'),

He heard of the virtue of Duke Mù of Qín
and desired to meet him,

He sold himself to a Qín traveler,
wearing coarse clothes and feeding cattle.
After a year,
Duke Mù knew of him,
raised him from below the mouths of cattle,
and placed him above the common people.
None in the state of Qín dared to look up to him.
Serving as Prime Minister of Qín for six or seven years,
he attacked Zhèng to the east,
established the ruler of Jìn three times,
and once rescued Jīng from disaster.
He issued edicts within the borders,
and the people of Bā offered tribute;
he bestowed kindness on the feudal lords,
and the Eight Róng came to submit.
Yóu Yú heard of this and,
knocked on the gate, requesting an audience.
When Wǔ Gǔ Dàfū (五羖大夫) was the minister of Qín (秦),
he would not ride when laboring,
nor would he raise an umbrella in the heat.
When traveling within the state,
he did not travel by carriage,
nor did he carry shields or spears.
His achievements were stored in the treasury,
and his virtue was passed on to future generations.
When Wǔ Gǔ Dàfū died,
the men and women of Qín wept,
children did not sing,
and those grinding grain did not coordinate their pestles.
This was the virtue of Wǔ Gǔ Dàfū.
Now, when you, sir, seek an audience with the King of Qín,
you rely on the favorite Jǐng Jiān (景監) as your patron;
this is not the way to gain a good reputation.
As minister of Qín,
you do not prioritize the welfare of the people,
but instead, you build the Jì Quē (冀闕) on a grand scale;
this is not the way to achieve merit.
You tattooed the teachers of the Crown Prince,
and cruelly injure the people with harsh punishments;
this is accumulating resentment and storing up trouble.
Education and transformation of the people penetrate deeper than commands,
and the people are quicker to emulate their superiors than to obey orders.
Now, you, sir, again promote heterodox ideas and disregard established customs;
This is not the way to teach.
You, sir, again face south and call yourself "Guǎrén" (the lonely one),
and daily put the noble young masters of Qín in ropes.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
"Even a rat has its limbs;
But a man without propriety;
A man without propriety,
Why does he not quickly die!"
Judging from the *Book of Poetry*,
this is not the way to live long.
Gōngzǐ Qián
has shut his door and not come out for eight years,
and you, sir, have killed Zhù Huān
and tattooed Gōngsūn Jiǎ.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
"He who gains the people thrives,
He who loses the people collapses."
These several things,
are not the way to gain the people.
When you, sir, go out,
there are over ten carriages behind,
the following carriages are loaded with armor,
those who are strong and have joined ribs serve as outriders,
and those who hold spears and wield halberds
run alongside the carriage.
If one of these things is not present,
you, sir, definitely do not go out.
The *Book of Documents* says:
"Those who rely on virtue prosper,
those who rely on force perish."
Your danger is like morning dew,
and yet you still wish to prolong your life?
Then why not return to the fifteen towns,
irrigate your garden in the countryside,
advise the King of Qin to promote scholars from hidden caves,
care for the elderly and protect orphans,
respect fathers and elder brothers,
reward the meritorious,
honor the virtuous,
and you can have a little peace.
You still covet the wealth of Shāng Yú,
indulge in the policies of the Qin state,
accumulate the resentment of the people,
once the King of Qin abandons his guests
and no longer attends court,
the reason why the Qin state accommodated you,
could it be insignificant?
Your demise can be awaited on tiptoes."
Shāng Jūn did not follow his advice.
Five months later, Duke Xiào of Qin died,
and the crown prince was established.
The followers of Gōngzǐ Qián accused Shāng Jūn of plotting rebellion,
and officials were sent to arrest Shāng Jūn.
Shāng Jūn fled to the pass,
wanting to stay at an inn.
The guest did not know that it was Lord Shang,
and said:
"The laws of Lord Shang state that
if an attendant has no proof
he will be punished."
Lord Shang sighed deeply and said:
"Alas, the defect of the law has actually reached this point!"
He left for Wei.
The people of Wei resented him for deceiving Gongzi Ang
and defeating the Wei army,
and did not accept him.
Lord Shang wanted to go to another state.
The people of Wei said:
"Lord Shang is a traitor to Qin.
Qin is strong, and if this traitor enters Wei,
and we do not return him, it is not allowed."
So they sent him to Qin.
After Lord Shang re-entered Qin,
he fled to Shangyi,
and along with his followers, he mobilized the troops of Shangyi
and went north to attack Zheng.
Qin sent troops to attack Lord Shang,
and killed him at Mianchi in Zheng.
King Hui of Qin dismembered Lord Shang by chariot
to make an example, saying:
"Let no one be like Shang Yang who rebels!"
And thus he destroyed the family of Lord Shang.
Grand Historian says:
"Shāng Jūn,
his natural disposition was harsh and unkind.
Judging by his desire to persuade Duke Xiào
with the arts of emperors and kings,
holding on to superficial theories,
it was not his true nature.
Moreover, he relied on favored ministers
to gain employment,
punished Gōngzǐ Qián,
deceived the Wèi general Áng,
and did not heed the words of Zhào Liáng,
which sufficiently demonstrate
Shāng Jūn's lack of kindness.
I have often read Shāng Jūn's 'Opening and Blocking' and 'Agriculture and War' books,
and they are similar to his actions.
In the end, he received a bad reputation in Qín,
and there was a reason for it!"
"Biography of Sū Qín, Number Nine"
Sū Qín was
a native of Luòyáng in Eastern Zhōu.
He went east to study with a teacher in Qí,
and learned from Master Guǐ Gǔ.
He traveled for several years,
He returned in great difficulty.
His brothers, sisters-in-law, wives, and concubines all secretly laughed at him,
saying:
"The custom of the people of Zhōu
is to manage property,
engage in industry and commerce,
and pursue a profit of twenty percent as their business.
Now, you abandon the fundamental and engage in verbal debate,
hardship, is it not fitting!"
Sū Qín heard this and was ashamed,
and felt sorry for himself,
so he closed himself in his room and did not come out,
taking out his books and reading them thoroughly.
He said:
"A scholar has already bowed his head and received books,
but cannot use them to attain honor and glory,
of what use are they, even if there are many!"
Thereupon, he obtained the Zhōu book "Yīn Fú" (Secret Accordance),
and bent over it, reading it.
After a year,
he went out and tested his ideas,
saying:
"This can be used to persuade the rulers of the present age."
He sought to persuade King Xiǎn of Zhōu.
The attendants of King Xiǎn were already familiar with Sū Qín,
and all looked down on him.
They did not trust him.
Then he went west to Qín.
Duke Xiào of Qín died.
He persuaded King Huì of Qín, saying:
"Qín is a country surrounded by four strategic barriers,
covered by mountains and bordering the Wèi River,
with the Guān Pass and the Yellow River to the east,
Hànzhōng to the west,
Bā and Shǔ to the south,
and Dài horses to the north.
This is a land blessed by Heaven.
With Qín's numerous soldiers and people,
and the teachings of military strategy,
you can swallow the world,
claim the title of Emperor, and govern."
The King of Qín said:
"My feathers are not yet grown,
I cannot fly high;
the patterns are not yet clear,
I cannot annex and combine."
He was in the process of executing Shāng Yāng,
hated sophists,
and did not employ him.
Then he went east to Zhào.
Marquis Sù of Zhào ordered his younger brother Chéng to be the Prime Minister,
styled Lord Fèngyáng.
Lord Fèngyáng did not appreciate him.
I went to travel to Yan,
and it was more than a year before I was received.
I said to Marquis Wén of Yān,
"To the east of Yan are Cháoxiǎn and
Liáodōng,
to the north are Línhú and
Lóufán,
to the west are Yúnzhōng and
Jiǔyuán,
to the south are Hūtuó and
Yìshuǐ.
The territory is over two thousand *lǐ* in area,
with several hundred thousand soldiers in armor,
six hundred chariots,
six thousand horses,
and grain enough to last for several years.
To the south are the abundance of Jiéshí and
Yànmén,
and to the north are the benefits of dates and chestnuts.
The people, even if they do not farm, have enough with dates and chestnuts.
This is what is called a 'heavenly treasury.'
"Moreover, in terms of peace and quiet,
without seeing armies routed and generals killed,

The reason why Yan is not invaded and does not have to wear armor and bear arms

Marquis Wen said,
"Your words are acceptable,
but my state is small,
bordered on the west by the powerful Zhao,
and close to Qi in the south.
Qi and Zhao are strong states.
If you must form an alliance to secure Yan,
I am willing to follow with my state."
Thereupon, he provided Sū Qín with carriages, horses, gold and silk, so that he could go to Zhao.
By then, Lord Fèng Yáng had already died,
so he then persuaded Marquis Sù of Zhao, saying:
"The ministers, officials, and common scholars of the world
all admire Your Highness's virtuous conduct
and have long wished to offer instruction and express their loyalty before you.
However,
Lord Fèng Yáng was jealous, and you did not employ people for their abilities,
so guests and wandering scholars dared not fully devote themselves to you.
Now that Lord Fèng Yáng has passed away,
you have now again become intimate with the scholars and people,
so I dare to offer my foolish thoughts."
"What I humbly advise for Your Highness's consideration is that
nothing is better than keeping the people secure and without incident,
and moreover, there is no need to trouble the people.
The foundation of keeping the people secure
The key lies in choosing alliances.
If alliances are chosen well, the people will be at peace.
If alliances are chosen poorly, the people will be uneasy for life.
Allow me to speak of external threats:
If Qí and Qín are two enemies, the people will not be at peace.
Relying on Qín to attack Qí will not bring peace to the people.
Relying on Qí to attack Qín will not bring peace to the people.
Therefore, the rulers who scheme against others
and attack other countries
often find it difficult to make pronouncements that sever other people's alliances.
I hope Your Majesty will be careful not to let such words come from your mouth.
Allow me to distinguish between white and black,
which is merely a difference between yin and yang.
If Your Majesty can truly listen to me,
Yān will surely offer lands with felt blankets, dogs, and horses.
Qí will surely offer the sea with fish and salt.
Chǔ will surely offer gardens with oranges and pomelos.
Hán, Wèi,
and Zhōngshān can all be made to offer revenues for your bath and hair washing.
And your noble relatives and elder brothers can all receive fiefs and titles.
Seizing territory and encompassing profits
is what the Five Hegemons sought by overthrowing armies and capturing generals.
Bestowing titles and noble rank upon relatives
is what Tāng and Wǔ fought for through banishment and regicide.
Now, Your Majesty can achieve both effortlessly.
This is what I desire for Your Majesty.
"If Your Majesty allies with Qín,
則 Qín bì ruò Hán,
Wèi; yǔ Qí,
zé Qí bì ruò Chǔ,
Wèi. Wèi ruò zé gē Héwài,
Hán ruò zé xiào Yíyáng,
Yíyáng xiào zé Shàngjùn jué,
Héwài gē zé dào bù tōng,
Chǔ ruò zé wú yuán.
Cǐ sān cè zhě,
bùkě bù shú jì yě.
"If Qin captures Zhidao,
then Nanyang is in danger;
if Qin coerces Han and surrounds Zhou,
then the Zhao will personally take up arms;
if Qin occupies Wei and takes Juan,
then Qi will certainly come to the Qin court.
If Qin wants to completely conquer Shandong,
then they must raise troops and march toward Zhao.
If Qin's armored soldiers cross the Yellow River and pass the Zhang River,
occupy Fanwu,
then the armies will surely fight below Handan.
This is what your subject worries about for you.
"At this time,
among the states in Shandong, none is stronger than Zhao.
Zhao's territory is more than two thousand li,
with armored soldiers numbering in the tens of thousands,
You have a thousand chariots,
ten thousand cavalry,
and grain enough to support you for several years.
To the west, you have Changshan Mountain,
to the south, the Rivers He and Zhang,
to the east, the River Qing,
and to the north, the state of Yan.
Yan is indeed a weak state,
not worth fearing.
Of all the states under heaven, Qin fears none so much as Zhao.
And yet, Qin dares not raise an army to attack Zhao,
why is that?
They fear that Han and Wei
will plot against them in the rear.
Thus, Han and Wei
are the southern shield of Zhao.
When Qin attacks Han and Wei,
there are no famous mountains or great rivers to defend them,
so Qin can gradually nibble away at their territory,
advancing until they reach their capital city and stop there.
Han and Wei cannot withstand Qin,
and will certainly become subjects of Qin.
Once Qin has no plan for Han and Wei,
then disaster will certainly befall Zhao.
This is what your servant is concerned about for you, my lord.
"Chén wén Yáo wú sān fū zhī fèn,
Shùn had no land of a *zhǐ chǐ*,
yet they possessed the world;
Yǔ had no gathering of a hundred men,
yet he reigned over the feudal lords;
The soldiers of Tāng and Wǔ did not exceed three thousand,
their chariots did not exceed three hundred,
their infantry did not exceed thirty thousand,
yet they established themselves as the Son of Heaven:
truly, they obtained the correct way.
Therefore, an enlightened ruler outwardly assesses the enemy's strength and weakness,
inwardly gauges the worthiness and unworthiness of his soldiers,
not waiting for the two armies to be facing each other, the opportunity for victory or defeat, survival or destruction, is already formed in his breast.
How could he allow himself to be obscured by the words of the masses and decide matters blindly!
"I have secretly examined the map of the world.
The lands of the feudal lords are five times greater than that of Qín,
I estimate the soldiers of the feudal lords are ten times greater than that of Qín.
If the six states were to unite,
and combine their strength to attack Qín from the west,
Qín would surely be defeated.
Now, to face west and serve them,
to become subjects of Qín.
To defeat others and to be defeated by others,
to make others subjects and to be subjects of others,
how can these be discussed in the same breath!
"Now, those who advocate alliances
All wanted to cede the lands of the feudal lords to give to Qín.
If Qín succeeds,
then they will build high terraces and pavilions,
beautiful palaces and houses,
listen to the sounds of the *yú* (笙, a reed pipe wind instrument) and *sè* (瑟, a plucked zither),
in front will be storied towers and raised walkways,
and behind will be tall, beautiful women.

Therefore, I hope that Your Majesty will carefully consider this.
I have heard that an enlightened ruler eliminates suspicion and removes slander,
cuts off the tracks of rumors,
and blocks the gates of factionalism.
Therefore, plans to honor the ruler, expand territory, and strengthen the army can be faithfully presented before you.
Therefore, I venture to plan for Your Majesty:
there is nothing better than uniting Hán,
Wèi, Qí,
Chǔ, Yān,
and Zhào to become close,
and to turn against Qín.
Order the generals and ministers of the world to meet on the banks of the Huán River,

If the six states formed an alliance to treat Qín as a guest,

There is no plan more advantageous than this."

Borrowing Sòng's seal,

With Qín and Qí united,

King Huái regretted it,

Lord Mèngcháng’s name was Wén,
his surname was Tián.
Wén’s father was called Lord Jìngguō, Tián Yīng.
Tián Yīng was
the youngest son of King Wēi of Qí and a half-brother of King Xuān of Qí.
Tián Yīng held office and managed affairs from the time of King Wēi.
Together with Marquis Chéng, Zōu Jì, and Tián Jì, he served as a general to rescue Hán and attack Wèi.
Marquis Chéng competed with Tián Jì for favor.
Marquis Chéng betrayed Tián Jì.
Tián Jì was afraid
and attacked the border towns of Qí.
He was not victorious
and fled.
Then King Wēi died.
King Xuān ascended the throne
and, knowing that Marquis Chéng had betrayed Tián Jì,
he recalled Tián Jì to serve as a general again.
In the second year of King Xuān,
Tián Jì, together with Sūn Bìn and
Tián Yīng, attacked Wèi
and defeated them at Mǎlíng,
capturing the crown prince of Wèi, Shēn, and killing the Wèi general Páng Juān.
In the seventh year of King Xuān,
Tián Yīng was sent as an envoy to Hán and Wèi.
Hán and Wèi submitted to Qí.
Yīng met with Hán Zhāo Hóu and
Wèi Huì Wáng south of Dōng'ē with Qí Xuān Wáng,

The following year,
he again met with Liáng Huì Wáng at Zhēn.
Wèi submitted to Qí.
In the same year,
Liáng Huì Wáng died.
In the ninth year of Xuān Wáng,
Tián Yīng became the chancellor of Qí.
Qí Xuān Wáng met with Wèi Xiāng Wáng in Xúzhōu to recognize each other as kings.
Chǔ Wēi Wáng heard of this and

The following year,

Tián Yīng sent Zhāng Chǒu to persuade Chǔ Wēi Wáng,

Tián Yīng served as chancellor of Qí for eleven years.
Xuān Wáng died,

In the third year after ascending the throne,
Tián Yīng was enfeoffed at Xuē.
Initially,
Tián Yīng had more than forty sons.
One of his concubines had a son named Wén,

Yīng told his concubine's mother:
"Do not raise him."
His mother secretly raised him.
When he grew up,

Tián Yīng angrily said to his mother,

Wén kowtowed,
